C0.note: Decided as ELIG by adjudication; the paper is a probabilistic voting model of incumbent policy choice.

C1.quote: Its equilibrium is characterized in Sect. 3.
C1.note: Incumbent's optimal policy choice (comparative statics) is the main result; welfare appears as good vs bad policy quality.

C2.1.value: none found (voting is probabilistic; no named input to a voting rule)

C2.2.note: Voters choose between two parties with a vote probability depending on estimated utilities and valence; no ballot format specified.

C2.3.quote: the voter can but estimate the effect a policy platform would have
C2.3.note: Voters have utilities and estimated utilities.

C2.4.quote: depends on the difference in the estimated utilities of the running platforms
C2.4.note: Vote probability is a function of estimated utility and valence; no statement about submission versus held attitude.

C3.1.note: Voters do not strategically misreport; the strategic agent is the incumbent.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: Input format is not RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH or PAIR.

C5.1.quote: the purely good policy is chosen
C5.1.note: Results evaluate policies as socially better or worse, based on voters' real utilities (Eq. 9).

C5.2.quote: the good policy is, indeed, better overall
C5.2.note: Evaluated on real utilities Uit, defined separately from estimated utilities that drive votes.

VOT.note: Voters follow a fixed probabilistic voting function with biased beliefs and retrospective valence.

CAN.quote_behav: chooses and implements a policy-platform for term t
CAN.quote_info: The incumbent is perfectly informed and chooses the policy platform
CAN.note: Incumbent maximises a payoff mixing office and policy motives. The opposition platform is fixed to bad.

DES.note: Contracts in Sect. 4.3 are exogenous; the designer's choice or objective is not modelled.

C7.1.quote: The incumbent is perfectly informed and chooses the policy platform
C7.1.note: CAN (incumbent) is STRAT; VOT is NONSTRAT.

C7.2.note: No reason is given for modelling voters as non-strategic; the voting model is inherited from Bischoff and Siemers (2013).

C8.1.quote: To deduce the political equilibrium, for simplicity and without loss of generality
C8.1.note: Incumbent's optimal choice is by first-order condition (single-agent optimisation, with the opposition's platform fixed as bad). It is not a standard game solution concept.

C8.2.quote: To deduce the political equilibrium, for simplicity and without loss of generality

claims.quote: there might be an advantage to keeping government in office
implementing incentive and threshold contracts emerges as a potentially valuable tool
it may nevertheless be optimal for an incumbent to select good long-term policies

C9.1.note: Claims on institutional design and welfare.

C9.2.quote: implementing incentive and threshold contracts emerges as a potentially valuable tool
C9.2.note: Needs the assumption that voters' real utility is the social welfare standard and that the incumbent is fully informed; the first is stated through Eq. 9, but the voters' non-strategic behaviour is not justified. The Sect. 5 federalism claims go beyond the model and rest on unmodelled assumptions.
